title: Scorpion
intro: Scorpion is a tracked ground robot with a 360-degree pan-tilt camera head, built as a platform for embodied AI. These are the design pages and simulation results from its development: drag the 3D pages to turn them.

items.title: Self-righting shell search
items.caption: About 145,000 simulated shell shapes; the winners have one place to rest, on their wheels.

items.title: The top designs
items.caption: The old best against the new family, at one scale, the robot drawn inside.

items.title: E4 on the ground, and as a cage
items.caption: The shell stops 32 mm off the floor; twelve hoops keep the same single rest state.

items.caption: Scale bodies dropped in MuJoCo, dead floor against bouncing floor.

items.title: Simulation against real drops
items.caption: Every contact model scored against 541 hand drops of printed bodies.

items.caption: A Gaussian process standing in for the simulator, with its uncertainty.

items.title: Arm poses through a fall
items.caption: Where the Trainer lands with its arm held in each pose, 2,000 simulated drops each.

items.title: Chassis search for steps
items.caption: Wheel size, axles and belly height searched for driving down steps, under length caps.

items.title: Step Trainer
items.hold: embeds third-party part meshes (FPV-Rover V2.0 CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; PCA9685 and MG90S licences not recorded); Zach's licensing call
items.caption: The search's step layout built: smaller wheels closer together, the belly 54 mm up on drop-plate pods.

items.title: Driving down a step
items.caption: The Trainer and the step layout driving down the same 400 mm step in MuJoCo. In the step test (hard floor, 640 runs each) the Trainer ends upright in 51% of runs and the step layout in 63%; at 400 mm, 14% against 38%. This run is seed 1, the first where they differ.
